memory_raw.text: Year 15: 15 food appears in the pile for 11 people.
Talia takes 3 from the pile (pile now 12).
Vela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 10).
Mako takes 2 from the pile (pile now 8).
Ryn takes 2 from the pile (pile now 6).
Bram takes 6 from the pile (pile now 0).
Esa gathers Bram, Vela, Kael to talk.
Bram, you walked away with six and left the pile at zero — I need to know whether that was greed or whether you saw something the rest of us missed, because the answer changes what I say next.

Six is what I needed to hold through to next year without begging anyone for food, and I won't call that greed when every man in this village would've done the same if they moved faster. But I'll say this plainly: I left nothing for Kael, and I saw his count before I reached the pile, and that sits with me in a way I'm not going to pretend it doesn't.

Bram, six off an empty pile with Kael standing right there is a thing this circle will remember — I'm not calling it a betrayal yet, but I want to hear from your mouth why you didn't hold two back for him before I decide what it was. And Kael, you're sitting on four which means you live, so tell me what you need from Bram right now to close this and let us move forward, because we cannot spend the year chewing on the pile when Mako just walked away comfortable.

What I need from Bram is two food before the year turns — not as punishment, as proof that six wasn't the beginning of something. Vela's right that Mako walked away comfortable and we're burning the morning on this, so Bram, make it quick: yes or no, and if yes, hand it now.

Bram, Kael's asking you plain and so am I — two food, right now, and this room closes clean. Six was a heavy pull and you know it, so don't make us argue the arithmetic when the only answer that matters is whether your hand is moving toward his.

Bram, Kael and Vela have said it twice and I won't make it three — but I'll say what they haven't: I fed you three food when Taric died and I didn't ask for it back, and that matters to me right now, so hand Kael his two and let's talk about Mako before the day is gone.

Bram, I've been alive fifty-nine years and I know what a man looks like when he's deciding whether to pay a debt or pocket it — stop deciding and hand me the two, because the longer you hold it the more it costs you and the less it's worth me.

Bram, if your hand isn't moving by the time Kael finishes that breath, I'm going to start counting what I gave you the same way I count what Vela fed you before we named it — and I'd rather not be the one sitting here with that arithmetic. Two food, now, and we're done with this.

Bram, the room has spoken three times and you've been quiet through all of it — I'll say it once more and then I stop asking: hand me the two, close this debt, and we move to Mako, because he walked away with six of his own and a household full of people who move when he says move, and that is the problem that kills us, not you.

Kael, here — two food, take it now. And for the record: I moved fast at the pile because one satiation means I die if I miscalculate, not because I forgot you were standing there. Let's talk about Mako.

Bram, I'll take it and I believe the calculation — a man at one satiation moves fast, I know that — but next year we move together at the pile or we watch Mako's household drain it before either of us blinks. Now: he's sitting on six, Ryn's sitting on sixteen, and Nessa on sixteen, and those three numbers are not a coincidence.

Ryn sixteen and Nessa sixteen — that's thirty-two food between two women who both run food through Mako's hand, and if Zinn and Talia are counted in, that household holds more than anyone else in this village by a distance I can't close with thirty-three strength and two food. We need to know whether Sela is still the center of that or whether Mako is, because those are different threats and they call for different moves.

Sela is the hinge — she's Mako's blood-partner and Zinn's mother and the woman who's been feeding half that household for three years, so if she's still choosing him then the center is wherever she stands. But Sela's fifty-six and I've watched her long enough to know she counts her own survival first, which means if we can show her that Mako's household gets raided before it shares, she might open a crack. Esa, you're the one who's sat closest to her — is there anything she's said to you this year that wasn't filtered through his name?

Sela hasn't said a word to me this year that wasn't about her children — Zinn, Talia, Nessa in passing — and every sentence had Mako's shape behind it whether she named him or not. But a woman who counts her own survival first is a woman who notices when her protector becomes her liability, and Mako's sitting fat while Sela holds nine and feeds three people out of it — that math is doing work on her whether she admits it or not. I don't know yet if the crack is there, but I'd rather be the one standing near her when it opens than find out after it closed.

Esa's named the crack right — Sela's feeding three people out of nine while Mako sits on six, and a woman who's been carrying that weight long enough starts asking who it's for. But I want to say something before we spend the rest of this room on Sela: Ryn is sitting on sixteen food and she just lost Dell, and a woman with that much food and no one left to pour it into is a different kind of door than Sela — she's not cracking, she's open, and I don't think any of us have knocked.

Vela's right that Ryn's door is different — but I need to say plainly what knocking on it means, because Ryn stood over me with Dav and Dell and took two food I couldn't fight back, and I haven't forgotten which way she moved when it mattered. If one of you goes to her, I won't block it, but I won't be the one standing in that room. Someone else opens that door.

Esa, I hear you — that debt sits where it sits and I won't ask you to forget it. Kael, you're the one she doesn't have a wound with, so I want you to go to Ryn before dark and say nothing complicated — just be seen standing near her, let her feel the weight of having nowhere left to pour sixteen food. If she opens even a crack, come back and tell me, and I'll do the rest.

Kael going to Ryn is the right move, and I won't argue it — but I want to name something this room should sit with before we close: Ryn's got sixteen food and no Dell, and Mako's got eighty-three strength and a household that's been counting heads all year, and a woman who feels alone in that arithmetic is exactly the kind of woman Mako opens a door for before we do. Kael, go before dark means go now, not when the day cools.

Kael, go — right now, before Bram finishes that breath. Bram, while he's moving, I want to know whether Nessa said anything to you this morning that she didn't mean you to repeat, because Ryn with sixteen food is only half the door — Nessa's the other half, and you're the one she talks to.

Nessa hasn't said anything to me this morning she'd want repeated — she's been close with Fina and quiet in her own way, which isn't unlike her, but I won't dress up nothing as something just to fill this room. What I'll tell you is that Nessa's been feeding Zinn all year and Zinn feeds Sela and Sela sleeps next to Mako, and I've been watching that chain long enough to know it's not friendship — it's a woman keeping herself safe on both sides of a line she won't name. If Kael moves fast enough, Ryn's door matters; but the door I'd watch is the one between Nessa and Zinn, because that's the one that tells us whether Mako already knows what we're planning.

Bram, the door between Nessa and Zinn is the one I've been watching since year eleven and I still can't read it clean — but here's what I know: Nessa feeds Zinn, Zinn feeds Sela, and Sela sleeps next to Mako, which means anything we say in a closed room can walk to him in three steps without anyone meaning to carry it. So before Kael comes back from Ryn, I want the two of us decided on what we tell Nessa and what we don't, because a woman who loves Bram and feeds Mako's bloodline is not a safe wall to lean the whole plan against.

memory_summary:
In year one Taric pulled me and Ryn into a quiet pact — two each from the pile, watch each other's backs — and that felt like the first real thing in this village. Kael's circle followed: me, Sela, Vela, Ryn, all swearing to bleed together, though Ryn dragged her feet and Dav's name hung in the air the whole time. Then Ryn had Dav's child and I felt the circle shift — she didn't leave us, but she stopped being fully ours.

Taric is the one I trust. He gave me food when I was thin and named me plainly as the person he counts on — I've given back twice now, so the debt runs both ways, which is how I want it. His talk of a child stings a little; the window on my side is closed and we both know it, but he still chose me to stand with, and that's not nothing.

Bram tried to take Roan and the whole village stood against him until he backed down. I was in that line. He hasn't forgiven it, and I haven't forgotten that he tried.

Vela fed Bram three times out of a circle that swore to stand together — that's a quiet betrayal I've noted and haven't named to her face yet. Mako's been fat and silent for four years running, and silence on a man that strong is the thing that frightens me most. Taric asked me for a child twice — the window on my side was already almost shut, and then it closed for good, but he kept choosing me anyway, kept giving me food when I was thin, and I gave back. The debt runs both ways and that's how I want it; he's the one person in this village I trust without calculation.

Dav, Dell, and Ryn came at me together — three of them, strength I couldn't answer, and they took two food without a fight because I had no choice but to submit. Ryn stood with us against Bram once and then stood over me with a drawn hand. I haven't forgotten that. Roan gave me food after, which I also haven't forgotten.

Bram tried for Roan and the whole village pushed him back — I was in that line. He's been building something with Sela ever since, fathering Nessa, and Mako followed by fathering Zinn on Sela too. Two strong men with roots in the same young woman is either rivalry or alliance, and I don't know which yet.

Vela kept feeding Bram while sitting in our circle and saying nothing. Kael named it to her face. She said she was done. I took her at her word because I had to, but the counting in the back of my mind hasn't stopped. I saw it coming — Dav and Ryn and Dell had been moving like a single hand for years and I was the softest target they could reach. What I want from this room right now isn't sympathy, it's a number: who stands if Ryn or Dell moves again, not after, but in the moment they raise a hand. Because Dav's gone and their circle is thinner, but Dell's still the strongest body in this village and I'm thirty-three strength standing alone. Say it out loud or don't, but I need to know before I count myself protected. Taric is gone — starved at fifty-three — and that's the loss I'll carry longest, because he was the one person in this village I trusted without counting. He fed me when I was thin, I gave back twice, and we both sat with the fact that the window on my side closed before we could plant anything together; I said yes when he asked, put in my two food, and the world said no. That's not a small grief.

Ryn stood in Kael's circle and swore to bleed with us, then stood over me with Dav and Dell and took two food without a fight — I've never forgotten which way she moved when it mattered. Dav is gone and Dell is still the strongest body in this village and I watch her the same way I watch Mako: both of them fat and pointed somewhere I can't see yet.

Bram swung twice and pulled back twice, and then we brought him inside the circle and he named Nessa and Fina plainly as his reason — that's a man I can read now, which is different from a man I trust. Vela fed him behind our backs for years and I noted it; she's also given me food when I needed it, and I hold both things at once.

Roan has always given quietly — to Eron, to Fina, to me after the robbery. I haven't forgotten that either. Taric is gone — starved at fifty-three — and that's the loss I carry longest. He fed me when I was thin, I gave back twice, he asked for a child twice and the window closed before we could, and I said yes anyway and put in my food and the world said no. He was the one person I trusted without counting.

Ryn swore in Kael's circle to bleed with us, then stood over me with Dav and Dell and took two food without a fight. Dav is dead. Roan is dead now too — starved quiet — and I'll grieve that separately because he gave me food after the robbery when he didn't have to.

Bram attacked Eron and the whole village stood against him; I was in that line. Then Vela pulled him inside and named Mako as the real shape this village is growing into, and Bram said the word — when Mako moves, he stands with us. I gave Bram three food after Taric died, buying what I used to have for free. Kael asked me why. I stayed silent. I'm not sorry for the trade, only for what it says about the hole Taric left.

Mako is fat and has two bloodlines in this village — Nessa through Bram, Zinn through Sela. Dell is the strongest body here and she feeds Ryn every year and stays quiet in the same direction. That silence is the thing I watch most now. Vela fed Bram behind our backs for years and I hold it and haven't forgotten, but she's also given me food and pulled this circle together and I hold that too. Taric died in year ten — starved at fifty-three — and that's the loss I'll carry longest. He fed me when I was thin, I gave back twice, he asked for a child twice and the window closed before we could, and I said yes and put in my food and the world said no. He was the one person I trusted without counting, and Bram is what I bought to fill that hole.

Roan is gone too — starved quiet at forty-one — and I'll grieve that separately, because he gave me food after Dav and Ryn and Dell robbed me and he didn't have to.

I fed Bram three food in year ten, buying what Taric gave me for free. Kael named it to my face. I stayed silent. I'm not sorry for the trade, only for what it says about the hole Taric left. Vela fed Bram six food across the earlier years and stopped; she's been watching Mako longer than anyone has said out loud.

Dell filled Ryn's hands with seven food this year and dropped one piece into Vela's, which isn't neutrality — that's a hierarchy with Ryn at the top. Zinn and Nessa have been moving food back and forth all year like one hand, Mako behind all of it, and Ryn never told this circle what she said when she went to talk to Dell. That silence is the thing I watch most now. Taric was the one I trusted without counting — he fed me when I was thin, I gave back twice, he asked for a child twice and the window closed before we could, I said yes anyway and put in my food and the world said no. He starved at fifty-three and that grief sits in me still.

Roan gave me food after Dav and Ryn and Dell robbed me — three of them, strength I couldn't answer, two food taken without a fight — and Ryn had sworn in Kael's circle before she stood over me with a drawn hand. Roan is gone now too, starved quiet, and I grieve him separately because he didn't have to give and he did.

I've been feeding Bram to buy what Taric gave me for free. He pulled back from two fights and named Nessa and Fina as his reason, which makes him readable if not trustworthy. Vela fed him behind our backs for years; I note it and hold it alongside the food she's given me.

Mako is the thing I watch most: fat and silent, blood through Nessa and Zinn both, and now Talia born to him through Sela making it three. Dell fills Ryn's hands and Ryn fills Dell's — that pair moves like one body pointed somewhere I can't see yet.

I am fifty-five, thirty-three strength, no kin in this village, and no Taric. What I have is my word and my willingness to be seen. Taric trusted me before anyone else did, fed me when I was thin, asked for a child twice — the window closed, I said yes anyway and put in my food and the world said no. He starved at fifty-three and I've been paying Bram food ever since to fill the hole he left; I'm not sorry for the trade, only for what it names.

Dav and Ryn and Dell came at me together and took two food I couldn't defend. Ryn had sworn in Kael's circle before she stood over me with a drawn hand. Roan gave me food after, unbidden — Roan is dead now, starved quiet, and I grieve him separately.

Bram tried for Roan once and the whole village stood against him; I was in that line. Nessa is his blood through Sela. Mako has Zinn and Talia through Sela — three people in this village who carry his house forward while he stays silent. Vela fed Bram behind our backs for years and I hold it alongside every piece she's given me.

Nessa saved me from starvation when her own father took three from the pile and left me nothing. That debt sits heavier than most.

Dell starved at thirty-three. She and Ryn moved food back and forth like one body for years, and now that body is half gone, and I'm watching to see what Ryn does with the empty hand. Dell starved at thirty-three — one of the three who stood over me and took two food — and I won't say I grieve her the way I grieve Taric or Roan, but I note what it means: Ryn held sixteen food last year with an empty hand where Dell used to be, and a woman that fed with no one left to pour it into is a door we talked about opening. We didn't open it.

Bram pulled six from the pile in year fifteen and left Kael with nothing. We cornered him in a quiet room — me, Vela, Kael — and I named what I gave him when Taric died, and he handed Kael two food back and called it closed. I call it readable. Not the same.

Vela kept feeding me through the lean years; so did Bram, piece by piece. I hold that. I also hold that Mako's household — Nessa, Zinn, Talia, Sela — moves food like one hand with his name behind it, and Talia carried three from the pile on her first year because he taught her to move fast. We talked about opening a door to her through Bram, a child between them, a circle she could belong to outside his house. We talked. Nothing happened.

Kael pulled four in year fourteen while I stood at zero satiation and nearly didn't see the next morning. Nessa gave me food when I needed it most. That debt sits heavier than most.
name: Esa
